content_voiceover: This table compares the four classic inherited platelet disorders that show up again and again on boards. Bernard Soulier syndrome gives you a low platelet count, often thirty to two hundred times ten to the third per microliter, with large platelets, and it's caused by mutations in G P one B A, G P one B B, or G P nine, inherited autosomal recessive. The defect is in the G P one b nine five complex, so platelets can't bind von Willebrand factor and adhesion fails. Contrast that with Glanzmann thrombasthenia, where the platelet count and size are both normal, but mutations in I T G A two B or I T G B three knock out the G P two b three a receptor, alpha two b beta three, so platelets can't aggregate even though they adhere fine. Chediak Higashi syndrome, caused by L Y S T mutations, gives normal or mildly low platelets with a dense granule deficiency that impairs storage and secretion, and remember this one comes with oculocutaneous albinism and giant cytoplasmic granules in leukocytes. Finally Wiskott Aldrich syndrome is X linked recessive, caused by W A S mutations, and it's the one with small platelets and thrombocytopenia from a cytoskeletal defect affecting platelet production and function. The classic triad to remember is thrombocytopenia, eczema, and recurrent infections.
keypoints: Bernard Soulier: low count, large platelets, GP1b-IX-V defect, autosomal recessive
Glanzmann thrombasthenia: normal count and size, GPIIb/IIIa defect, impaired aggregation
Chediak-Higashi: LYST mutation, dense granule deficiency, albinism association
Wiskott-Aldrich: X-linked, small platelets, cytoskeletal defect, triad with eczema and infection
keypoint_voiceover: Four inherited platelet disorders. Bernard Soulier is large platelets with a G P one b defect and impaired adhesion. Glanzmann thrombasthenia has normal size platelets but a G P two b three a defect causing impaired aggregation. Chediak Higashi involves L Y S T mutations with dense granule deficiency, linked to albinism. And Wiskott Aldrich is X linked with small platelets, a cytoskeletal defect, and the classic triad of thrombocytopenia, eczema, and recurrent infections.
